facts.statement: The genus Pantydraco was established by Galton, Yates, and Kermack in 2007.
The genus is based on a partial juvenile skeleton that was previously classified as Thecodontosaurus.
facts.quote: It is based on a partial juvenile skeleton once thought to belong to Thecodontosaurus.

facts.statement: Pantydraco had a long tail that tapered at the end but was broad at the hip joint.
facts.quote: The creature had a long tail that tapered towards the end and was broad at the hip joint.

facts.statement: Its forelimbs were adapted for grasping, while its hindlimbs supported its body weight.
facts.quote: The forelimbs of the dinosaur were developed for grasping while the hindlimbs were adapted for supporting the creature's body weight.

facts.statement: The hands possessed three movable digits with a fourth digit embedded within them.
facts.quote: The hands had three movable digits while the fourth digit was embedded.

facts.statement: Juvenile fossils of Pantydraco are estimated to have been between 0.7 and 1 meter tall.
facts.quote: The juvenile fossils' estimated height is from about 0.7 to 1 m.

facts.statement: Adult Pantydraco are believed to have reached a length of about 3 meters.
facts.quote: Adults are believed to have been about 3 m long.

facts.statement: The estimated weight for an average adult Pantydraco is about 50 kilograms.
facts.quote: The estimated weight for an average adult of this species of dinosaurs is about 50 kg.

facts.statement: Adam Yates named the species Thecodontosaurus caducus in 2003 based on fossil material NHMUK PV RUP 24.
facts.quote: In 2003, Adam Yates named the new species Thecodontosaurus caducus for NHMUK PV RUP 24

facts.statement: The fossil material used to describe Pantydraco had been known in scientific literature since 1983.
facts.quote: This material had been known in the scientific literature since 1983

facts.statement: The fossils were originally discovered in 1952 by Kermack and Robinson.
facts.quote: discovered in 1952 by Kermack and Robinson.

facts.statement: The region where Pantydraco lived was a characteristic wetland during the Triassic period.
facts.quote: The Pant-y-ffynnon region was a characteristic wetland during the Triassic.

facts.statement: Researchers consider Pantydraco to have been probably omnivorous, representing a transition from carnivory to herbivory.
facts.quote: Pantydraco is considered to have most probably been omnivorous, being at the transition from carnivory to herbivory in the sauropodomorph lineage.

facts.statement: It is probable that Pantydraco walked bipedally.
facts.quote: It is probable that Pantydraco would have walked bipedally.

facts.statement: Pantydraco lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 204 million years ago in the Rhaetian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió en el Triásico superior, hace aproximadamente 204 millones de años, en el Rhaetiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Pantydraco is classified within the superorder Dinosauria, order Saurischia, and suborder Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria ordo: Saurischia subordo: Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: Pantydraco is generally considered basal within Sauropodomorpha, closely related to Thecodontosaurus.
facts.quote: Pantydraco generalmente se encuentra basal en Sauropodomorpha, todavía junto con Thecodontosaurus.

facts.statement: The time range for Pantydraco is estimated from 237 to 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species name caducus means "fallen" in Latin, referring to the hypothesis that the animal fell into a fissure fill and died there.
rejected.quote: caducus, means "fallen" in Latin, referring to the assumption that it fell into a fissure fill (quarry) and died there.
